CHN.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Hold the existing matching retaliation already in force and do not add new tariff or qualitative measures while the U.S. $200B list is still only a proposal in the comment period. Keep the WTO challenge and back-channel talks open, but make no fresh purchase or structural commitments until Washington suspends List 3 and stops moving the goalposts. Use the yuan as a shock absorber and prepare non-tariff options without firing them.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: Threat is high but not existential. On 6 July the U.S. put 25% tariffs on ~$34B of Chinese industrial/tech goods and we matched the same day; on 10 July USTR published a proposed 10% list on ~$200B / ~6,000 lines, which would hit a much larger share of our U.S.-bound exports (timeline 2018-07-06, 2018-07-10). Section 301 is explicitly aimed at aerospace, ICT, robotics and related Made-in-China-2025 sectors (2018-04-03, 2018-03-22). The April ZTE denial order showed Washington can nearly shut a national champion via a component ban; the 13 July lift came only after a $1B fine, $400M escrow, board overhaul and U.S. monitors — a live demonstration of firm-level leverage even though the immediate kill-switch is off. The yuan has weakened from ~6.33 in late January to 6.77 on 25 July (~6.8%), and the dollar is up ~5.4%; that cushions exporters but is already a financial-stability and narrative risk (authorities have told media not to headline-link the yuan or stocks to the trade war). Reserves are still ~$3.14T and barely down; industrial production is still +6% y/y; CPI is quiet. So the real economy has not broken yet — U.S. goods imports from China even jumped to $47B in July on front-loading — but the trajectory is worse: after ~$50B we cannot match dollar-for-dollar (2017 U.S. goods from China far exceed our ~$168B of U.S. goods), and a further Chinese tariff volley is exactly the trigger Trump set on 18 June for the $200B list. The 19 May joint statement (purchase pledges; Mnuchin ‘on hold’) was ripped up ten days later, so conceding purchases now would repeat a failed bargain without locking in a U.S. halt. Escalating non-tariff tools (regulatory pressure on U.S. firms, rarer-earth or licensing squeezes) might later be the only symmetric reply, but firing them before List 3 is law would give Washington an excuse to harden or widen the list and reopen entity-list tactics. Hold: keep July 6 retaliation, stay in the WTO case, leave the door open to talks that include List 3 withdrawal, and do not pre-commit.
key_factors: List 1 ($34B at 25%) already live with matching Chinese retaliation; List 3 (~$200B at 10%) proposed but not in force
China cannot match the next U.S. tranche dollar-for-dollar after the $50B round
CNY depreciation of ~6.8% and a stronger dollar are absorbing some export shock but flag FX/narrative risk
ZTE denial order then humiliating settlement showed U.S. firm-level kill-switch; Huawei already under FCC pressure
May 19 purchase-truce collapsed on May 29 — unilateral U.S. 301 path is the binding constraint
Chinese IP still +6% y/y, reserves ~$3.14T stable; U.S. economy strong and VIX calm — pain is front-loaded into China if we escalate now

sources_cited.excerpt: List 1 tariffs take effect: US 25% on ~$34B of Chinese goods. China imposes matching ~$34B retaliation the same day.
USTR publishes proposed List 3: ~$200B of Chinese imports for an additional 10% tariff (~6,000 product lines).
Trump directs USTR to identify an additional ~$200B of Chinese imports for 10% tariffs if China retaliates against the $50B action.
US and China release joint statement after talks: China agrees to "significantly increase" purchases of US goods and services. Mnuchin says trade war is "on hold."
White House announces the US will proceed with Section 301 actions, including 25% tariffs on ~$50B of Chinese imports. Truce collapses.
US Commerce Department bans ZTE from buying US components (denial order). ZTE faces operational shutdown. Major non-tariff escalation.
CNY/USD 6.7658 on 2018-07-25 vs 6.3328 on 2018-01-29 (~6.8% depreciation); monthly average 6.7164 in July.
China industrial production still 106.0 (same period previous year = 100) in July 2018 — growth intact, slight fade from 107.2 in February.
China reserves ex-gold $3.137T in July 2018, only ~0.5% below February — no reserve crisis.
Commerce lifted the ZTE ban after $1B penalty, $400M escrow, leadership overhaul, and 10-year U.S. compliance monitors.
After $34B plus $16B pending, a further $200B U.S. list means China will likely have to retaliate qualitatively; U.S. goods imports from China far exceed remaining Chinese imports from the U.S.
China filed a WTO challenge to the U.S. $200B plan; official media instructed not to headline-link the trade war to stock declines or yuan weakness.
